title: fix(automation): a screen flow refuses a required field of only spaces at the field, and a screen refusal reaches the user at its fields in their language
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuQVQdf3PvoJbKFFCUA4gwJB)_

Fixes #37526

## What changes

**Client: spaces are no answer.** The flow screen dialog's `required` check (`FlowRunner.tsx`, new exported `isUnanswered`) counts a string that is empty once trimmed as missing, as the engine's `isPresent` does. Three spaces in a required field are refused under the field with the same `validation.required` message an empty field gets, focus moves there, and no resume request is made. An unchecked `false` and `0` stay answers.

**Wire: a screen refusal names its fields in a structured slot.** `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` now carries `error.details.fields`: one `{ field, code, message }` per violated screen field, `code` an ADR-0114 `FieldErrorCode` (`required`, `invalid_type`, `invalid_value`, `min_value`, `max_value`, `unknown_field`). These are the entries `VALIDATION_FAILED` already serves in the same slot, and each parses under `FieldErrorSchema`.
- `@objectstack/spec`: `AutomationResult` gains the optional `fields?: FieldError[]`, set with `code: 'INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT'` only, and `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data` mirrors it as `z.array(FieldErrorSchema).optional()` (the #13078 identity pin `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` holds the two equal). The generated reference page `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` is regenerated.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: `refuseInvalidScreenInput` fills it from the `validateScreenInputs` issues it already computed.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: `classifyResumeResult` serves it as `details.fields` on that row only, so the REST door and MCP `resume_run` answer it alike. Another row, or an empty list, serves no details, as before.
- `error.message` is byte-identical: the sentence with the declared field names stays for logs and API callers.

**Console: the refusal is placed at its fields, in the user's language.** `interpretFlowResponse` reads the findings (`screenInputFindings`, `{ field, code }` only) onto a failed outcome's new `screenInput`. `FlowRunner` marks each on-screen field named, by the label it shows and in the display language: `required` → `validation.required`, a bound → `validation.min` / `max` when the field declares it, anything else → new `flowRunner.fieldNotAccepted`. Focus moves to the first. The banner and toast read new `flowRunner.invalidScreenInput` instead of the engine's sentence, also from a server that sends no findings. Both keys are in all 11 locales. The #36831 re-read of the run before a retry is unchanged and still runs first.

Docs: `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` § *A `screen` resume is checked against the declared fields* documents `details.fields` and the runner's behaviour.

## Why

The card measured on 18.6.0 (zh-CN console, HotCRM Close Case): three spaces in the required `resolution` passed the dialog, the engine trimmed and refused, and the dialog showed `Invalid screen input: Screen field "resolution" is required — declared fields: 'resolution', 'resolved_by_article'` verbatim. Premise re-read on `main` 33a31dc7: the dialog's check did not trim (`FlowRunner.tsx:848-849`), the engine's does (`screen-input-contract.ts:58-59`), and the refusal envelope carried only `details.code`. The dialog's own header said why the sentence stayed in the banner: "the envelope names no field in a structured slot, so placing it at a field would mean parsing prose". This PR adds that slot instead of parsing.

## Verification

- `service-automation` `builtin/screen-input-whitespace-fields-37526.test.ts` (real `AutomationEngine`, Close Case screen): `'   '` refused `required` with `fields` and the unchanged sentence, the pause kept; one entry per violated field (`required`, `min_value`, `unknown_field`); a real answer resumes with no `fields`.
- `runtime` `domains/automation-resume-screen-input-fields-37526.test.ts` (REST resume door): `details.fields` served, `message` unchanged, the envelope parses under `ApiErrorSchema` and each entry under `FieldErrorSchema`; an empty list and another row serve no details. `automation-resume-refusal-codes.test.ts` (every row: empty details when the engine sends no fields) and `mcp-resume-run.test.ts` stay green.
- `app-shell` `FlowRunner.whitespaceRequired-37526.test.tsx` (7 tests): spaces refused at the field in en and zh with no request; findings placed by label (`Resolution is required`, `Hours must be at least 0`), focus on the first, catalog banner and toast, no API field name on screen; zh banner and `fieldNotAccepted` message; no findings → catalog banner, no field marked; editing retires the message and the resubmit completes. **Ablation:** against `main`'s `FlowRunner.tsx` and `flowResponse.ts`, 7 of 7 red.
- Two existing pins moved, same intent (a retryable refusal keeps the screen, values and Submit): `FlowRunner.requiredAtField-26882.test.tsx` and `FlowRunner.resumeResult.test.tsx` asserted the engine's sentence in the banner. They now assert the catalog sentence, and that the engine's is absent.
- Suites: service-automation `screen` + `resume` 30 files / 345 tests; runtime `resume` + `http-dispatcher` 40 / 825; client `automation-resume` 1 / 8; ui `i18n` + all `FlowRunner*` + `flowResponse` 132 / 2237 (13 skipped).
- spec: `api/automation-api*` + `contracts` 58 files / 585 tests; `check:generated` 14 of 14 green (incl. `check:test-typecheck`, which caught the missing Zod mirror first).
- `tsc --noEmit`: service-automation and runtime exit 0. app-shell `tsc` and `tsconfig.test.json` show no error in the changed files (the 6 / 7 errors are in untouched files, from stale local dists of other ui packages). eslint on the changed files: 0 errors.
- `overlap-check` clean against `origin/main` d92684a7 and 1 PR head (#37422, shares the locale files and the generated reference page, merges cleanly).

## Small decisions (dev thread)

- **What `details.fields[].message` carries, and why it is there.** The claim said the findings would carry no message with author keys. The PR uses the existing `FieldErrorSchema` entry `{ field, code, message }` instead of a new two-member shape, because `message` is required there and the slot is the one `VALIDATION_FAILED` already fills. The `message` is the engine's English line for that one finding, verbatim, and it is a substring of `error.message`, which this PR does not change: `Screen field "resolution" is required`, `Screen field "hours" must be at least 0`, `Unknown screen field "nickname" — not declared on this screen`. So it names the field by its machine name, which `field` names anyway. For `unknown_field` it echoes the key the CALLER sent. It never carries the declared-fields list, the other fields' names, or a value. Nothing new reaches the wire: every string in `details.fields` was already in the same response's `error.message`. The console never renders `message`. `screenInputFindings` keeps only `{ field, code }`, and the text under a field is the console's own catalog sentence with the field's label. The server log is unchanged: the findings ride its structured slot (`{ issues }`), never its message (#6654).
- **Bounds read the field's own declaration.** A `min_value` / `max_value` finding reads as `validation.min` / `max` with the limit taken from the screen field's declared `min` / `max`, because the engine's entry carries no constraint. Without that declaration it falls back to `flowRunner.fieldNotAccepted`.
- **Toast kept beside the banner.** On an engine refusal the dialog keeps the toast plus banner it already raised for every resume failure (`c40f3b8ca`), now with the catalog sentence. Only the client-side required refusal raises no toast (#26882), and that is unchanged.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Owed: L1 (seat); L2 (seat arranges: the new optional `details.fields` member on `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` and `AutomationResult.fields`).

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (The wire member is Zod on `TriggerFlowResponseSchema`, element `FieldErrorSchema`; the contract interface mirrors it.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (`gen:docs`; `check:generated` 14 of 14 green against a fresh build)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
